history_note: Single published reading; no time series on the card.
name: IEA World Energy Investment 2026: upstream oil falls for a third year, gas spending at a ten-year high
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: annual capex budgets turn into sanctioned projects and then into protection-relay orders for platforms, terminals and compressor stations roughly 12-24 months later. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: IEA, World Energy Investment 2026 (reported by IENE)
source.access: Public news report of the IEA release, free

classification_rationale: Oil supply investment is falling while gas investment, mostly US LNG, is rising, so the total mixes a cyclical oil leg with a structural gas leg. Relay demand follows the gas and LNG leg more than the oil leg.

value.label: global natural gas investment in 2026, up over 10% and a ten-year high; oil supply investment below USD 500 bn

excerpt: Less than $500 billion will be invested in oil supply. [...] Natural gas growth largely from U.S. LNG projects

history_note: Single published reading; no time series on the card.
name: EIA STEO October 2026: Brent at USD 105 in Q4 2026, falling to USD 84 on average in 2027
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: producer cash flow follows the oil price within quarters and capex plans follow cash flow within one to two years, so the price leads orders by roughly 6-12 months. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026

classification_rationale: A forecast price path driven by a Middle East supply disruption and inventory draws is a cyclical driver of customer cash flow. The measure is read as customer capex capacity, not as an input cost to ABB: the fall from USD 105 to USD 84 lowers it.

value.label: forecast Brent spot average for 2027, after USD 105/b expected in 4Q26

excerpt: We now forecast the Brent crude oil spot price will average $105 per barrel (b) in 4Q26 [...] We expect the Brent spot price will fall to an average of $84/b next year.

history_note: Single published reading; no time series on the card.
name: Statistics Norway: oil and gas investment NOK 275 bn in 2026, NOK 227 bn expected for 2027
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: the survey reports operators' own investment plans for the next two years; relay demand for platforms and subsea tie-backs follows project execution within about 6-18 months. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: Statistics Norway investment survey (reported by Offshore Energy Digital / Reuters)
source.access: Public news report of the SSB release, free

classification_rationale: The 2026 level is revised up, but the 2027 estimate is lower than 2026. A step down from a high level, not a collapse; the base of production drilling on operating fields remains.

value.label: expected 2027 oil and gas investment in Norway (2026: NOK 275 bn; previous 2027 estimate: NOK 207 bn)

excerpt: The Nordic country's biggest business sector now expects to invest 275 billion Norwegian crowns ($28.97 billion) in 2026, up from 266 billion seen in May [...] Next year, investments are expected to decline to 227 billion crowns, above the 207 billion crowns seen previously

name: Baker Hughes: US oil and gas rig count at 603, 10% above a year earlier
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: the rig count is an early indicator of drilling output; wellsite and midstream electrical orders follow with a lag of roughly 3-9 months. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: Baker Hughes weekly rig count (reported by BOE Report / Reuters)

classification_rationale: Rig counts react to the oil price within months and reverse with it; this reading is cyclical.

value.label: US total oil and gas rigs, week to 16 October 2026 (oil 459, gas 133, other 11)

excerpt: The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, held steady at 603 in the week to October 16. [...] Baker Hughes said that put the total rig count up 55 rigs, or 10% above this time last year.

short: ABB Q2 oil and gas comment
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: a supplier's own order commentary reports orders already booked, so it is close to coincident with relay demand. Verify with ABB.]

name: PwC: high-capacity transformer lead times up to four years (US grid, shared electrical supply chain)
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: long lead times on shared electrical equipment delay energisation of oil and gas sites and push relay deliveries; the effect is felt within the project schedule, about 6-18 months. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: pv magazine USA, U.S. transformer market faces severe supply constraints as lead times extend to four years

classification_rationale: Capacity of transformer factories changes over years, not quarters. The card concerns the US grid; oil and gas projects compete for the same equipment but the card does not measure oil and gas orders.

value.label: longest lead time for high-capacity transformers, according to PwC analysts

excerpt: Long transformer lead times are now dictating power project schedules across the country. [...] Lead times for high capacity units to as long as four years, according to analysts from PwC.

name: European Parliament backs a three-year delay to EU methane rules for oil and gas imports
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: monitoring and abatement obligations create equipment projects about two years before enforcement; a delay moves them out. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: Hydrocarbon Processing, European Parliament votes to approve three-year delay on EU methane rules

classification_rationale: A parliamentary position, not yet final law. It lowers the near-term pull on methane monitoring and abatement equipment but does not remove the regulation.

value.label: delay approved by Parliament; importers would have until 31 May 2031 to show equivalent monitoring, reporting and verification

excerpt: The European Parliament voted on Thursday to approve a three-year delay to the EU's methane emissions rules for oil and gas imports.

name: EIA: Middle East shut-in oil production easing, attacks on the Saudi East-West pipeline
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: a regional disruption changes customer investment decisions and shipping risk within about two quarters. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026

classification_rationale: Hostilities and shut-ins are an event-driven disruption, not a trend. Direction is read as the effect on ABB's Middle East customer activity (negative while disrupted); the card does not claim a rebuild order wave.

value.label: EIA forecast Brent in 4Q26 during the Middle East disruption; regional shut-in production in September lowest since the onset of hostilities

excerpt: The attacks on the East-West pipeline in Saudi Arabia highlight the potential for continued volatility in physical oil flows and oil prices amid ongoing withdrawals of oil inventories globally.

name: Wood Mackenzie: 225 Mtpa of LNG under construction after a record year of FIDs in 2025
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: liquefaction trains already sanctioned order switchgear and protection in the build phase, roughly 1-3 years before start-up. Verify with ABB.]

source.name: Wood Mackenzie via LNG Industry, Five global gas and LNG themes to look out for in 2026

classification_rationale: Sanctioned liquefaction projects are multi-year builds with contracts and financing in place; they do not unwind with a quarterly price move. Timing of orders within the build is uncertain.

value.label: LNG supply under construction; 2025 record FIDs: nine projects totalling 72 Mtpa

excerpt: 2025 was a record year for final investment decisions, with nine projects totalling 72 million tpy [...] with 225 million tpy of LNG supply currently under construction, the expectation is for lower LNG prices
